_incidents.description: Launched 1:2 and 1:3 gaussian:mask sanity runs (both corruption_mode=mixture) within the same second. corruption_sanity.sbatch keys RESULTS_DIR only by CORRUPTION_MODE (not job ID), and train.py's experiment_index = len(glob(RESULTS_DIR/*)) is a classic TOCTOU race -- both processes computed index=002 and wrote to the SAME .../corruption_sanity_mixture/002-EqM-B-2-Linear-velocity-None/ directory, confirmed via both jobs' logs showing identical 'Experiment directory created at ...002-...' at the same timestamp (2026-07-07 11:31:44). Both jobs ran to completion (exit 0, 8 checkpoints present at steps 5000-40000) but each checkpoint file's actual weights (1:2 vs 1:3 mask ratio) are INDETERMINATE -- whichever process's torch.save() won the race for that step. These checkpoints must NOT be used for eval; discarding entirely.
_incidents.fix: corruption_sanity.sbatch RESULTS_DIR now includes ${SLURM_JOB_ID} unconditionally, eliminating any possibility of two jobs sharing a results dir regardless of corruption_mode or submission timing. Committed 17217f4.
_incidents.lesson: Never launch two jobs with the same corruption_mode close together without a job-scoped results dir -- this applies retroactively to the earlier arm-B mixture run (job 28888839) and the original 3-arm mixture run (job 28814819), which were NOT launched concurrently with same-mode siblings so are believed unaffected, but the results-dir-collision risk existed for all of them before this fix.
_incidents.recovery_action: Relaunched both runs cleanly as jobs 29233398 (1:2) and 29233403 (1:3) with the fixed sbatch.
_incidents.root_cause: corruption_sanity.sbatch RESULTS_DIR keyed by CORRUPTION_MODE only; train.py experiment_index has no locking/atomicity for concurrent writers to the same results_dir.
_incidents.title: Results-dir race: two concurrent same-corruption-mode jobs silently mixed checkpoints

completed_runs.final_metric: INVALIDATED (D FD K=4). Ran with a broken frozen_label_dropout: models.py passes the EqM MODULE's training flag to y_embedder, so emb.eval() never disabled token_drop. Labels were pre-dropped then re-dropped with fresh randomness every forward, and token_drop draws PER ROW, so phi(z+hu) and phi(z-hu) for the same sample got independent conditioning even inside one stacked forward -- corrupting ~10% of FD pairs at dropout_prob=0.1. Any Arm-D conclusion from these runs is an artifact. 39078779 additionally OOM'd on an 80 GB A100 because K=4 stacks 2*K*B activations. Superseded by the clean reruns 39090540/41/42.

completed_runs.description: Throughput probe after the CORRECTED storage diagnosis: single GPU, global batch 64, 40 steps, log every 5, NUM_WORKERS=12, running ALONE. Establishes the achievable steps/sec on this filesystem so Phase II-A can be staged at a concurrency the ~3 MB/s-per-stream ImageNet path can actually sustain.
completed_runs.error: torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError in diffusers autoencoder_kl.encode, batch 64 on a 19.62 GiB MIG slice
completed_runs.final_metric: FAILED with CUDA OOM in vae.encode -- but DIAGNOSTICALLY VALUABLE, and it separates two independent problems. (a) Data loading took 5 SECONDS (21:56:52 dataset -> 21:56:57 training), so the ImageNet filesystem is fine once jobs are not competing; the earlier stalls were self-inflicted I/O contention from 12 concurrent jobs. (b) This failure is unrelated: global batch 64 on ONE gpu_test MIG slice (19.62 GiB) OOMs inside the VAE encoder, which allocates 2 GiB on top of 18.5 GiB in use. Partition/batch mismatch, not a code fault -- seas_gpu's 80 GB cards hold 64 images/GPU comfortably.
completed_runs.gate: Produces steps/sec -> relaunch Phase II-A staged in small batches at that concurrency. Still no progress alone with 12 workers -> escalate, since 27 files/s measured would then not explain it.

completed_runs.description: DIAGNOSTIC: BTM vector arm on ONE GPU at global batch 32 -- the repository's own proven recipe -- 60 steps, log every 10. Tests the BTM loss path without DDP, and doubles as the fallback Phase II configuration. Now running ALONE after all competing jobs were cancelled, which makes it a direct test of the filesystem-contention hypothesis.
completed_runs.final_metric: CANCELLED. Never reached training. Confirmed the stall is NOT DDP and NOT the BTM loss: a single-GPU run at the repo's own recipe (batch 32) took >14 min without loading its FIRST batch. Root cause isolated to ImageNet storage: on the holylfs06 training tree, `ls` of one class directory and `cat` of 32 files each exceed 120s, while `ls` of the dataset ROOT returns in 4ms -- cold metadata/data reads are pathologically slow, warm ones are instant.
completed_runs.gate: If it now produces steps/sec logs alone on the filesystem, the stall was self-inflicted concurrency and Phase II-A relaunches staged in small batches. If it still stalls alone, the ImageNet path itself is the problem and an alternative data path must be used.

completed_runs.gate: Gate 0 diagnostic: is the field-error gap a real VJP bug or GPU precision noise
completed_runs.gate_verdict: DEFINITIVE: the manual reverse-mode VJP implementation is mathematically exact at real EqM-B/2 scale with real trained weights -- there is no mechanism bug anywhere in the reverse chain (attention, LayerNorm, MLP, AdaLN modulation, residual/gate bookkeeping, patch-embed, final scalar head all verified simultaneously end-to-end). The ~1.5-1.8e-4 rel_error seen in every real-GPU FP32 Gate 0 run (job 37520759 baseline, 37521466 retune#1 FP32-promotion, 37522251 retune#2 SDPA-backend-fix -- all three landed within noise of each other) is therefore pure GPU floating-point precision effect (most likely TF32 tensor-core matmul accumulation compounding over 12 SiT blocks x ~7 matmuls/block), not a code defect. All 3 authorized retunes (1 standard + 2 user-granted) are now exhausted with a conclusive diagnosis: Gate 0's literal <1e-4 threshold, applied to an FP32/TF32 GPU training regime at this network depth, is a precision target the hardware's default numerics cannot reliably hit even with provably-correct code. Escalating to user: either (a) relax Gate 0's threshold to something achievable under FP32/TF32 at this depth (e.g. <5e-4, informed by the observed ~1.7e-4 typical value plus margin), (b) force full FP32 (allow_tf32=False) process-wide for Gate 0 evaluation specifically as a stricter apples-to-apples check (not yet tried -- would very likely close the gap given the FP64 result, but changes what Gate 0 is actually measuring relative to real bf16/TF32 training conditions), or (c) treat cosine>0.999999 + loss_rel_diff<1e-4 as the operative pass criteria instead of raw field rel_error, since those two are already comfortably passing and are arguably the more decision-relevant metrics for whether training will work. No code changes needed regardless of which option is chosen -- the implementation itself is proven correct.

completed_runs.description: Retune #2 of Gate 0 (of 2 additional retunes explicitly authorized by the user beyond AGENTS.md's normal 1-retune rule, specifically to bisect and fix the remaining VJP/kernel discrepancy): force MATH-backend SDPA (torch.backends.cuda.sdp_kernel(enable_flash=False, enable_math=True, enable_mem_efficient=False)) inside fb_direct/trainer.py:exact_field_audit and the gate0 script's model_direct forward call. Hypothesis: forward_energy_with_cache's manual two-pass-softmax attention is bit-identical to SDPA's MATH backend (verified 1.6e-16 rel error in FP64 locally) but timm's Attention.forward has use_fused_attn()=True by default on CUDA, so the autograd ground truth in exact_field_audit was silently using a different fused kernel than the manual cache reconstruction.

Originally job 29403281 on seas_gpu (ETA ~18:16, ~4.5h queue wait) -- moved to gpu_test (idle, immediate start) for a guaranteed ~6h total instead of a queue-estimate gamble.

Cancelled before wasting the full 11h on an inevitable walltime kill; resubmitted as job 34314943 on seas_gpu (no cap) with --time=20:00:00. Root cause: make_structured_mask's per-sample Python dispatch loop (transport/corruption.py) has real per-step overhead vs the vectorized elementwise mask_corrupt -- consistent across block/patch/region families, not unique to the region flood-fill. Same overhead affects the mixture arm (gm) since mixture_sample computes structured_mask_corrupt for the full batch every step regardless of per-sample arm assignment (same pattern as existing mask/fourier/blur/downsample arms in mixture_sample, not a new anti-pattern). All structured_mask/mixture arms routed to seas_gpu with 20h walltime; gaussian-only arms stay on gpu_test/seas_gpu with standard 11h.

completed_runs.final_metric: CLEAN NULL RESULT for Hypothesis A, first decisive result after 5 prior null/inconclusive diagnostics. R_direct=2.58 (spike/control A_backbone ratio, own-selection) vs R_none=2.49 -- statistically indistinguishable, Delta=0.034 log-units, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.119, 0.279] comfortably includes 0. Both models show ~2.5x normalized Jacobian amplification on their own hard-selected batches -- since A=||J^T(r/||r||)|| is residual-magnitude-normalized BY CONSTRUCTION, this rules out Hypothesis C (residual-size artifact) directly and supports Hypothesis B (shared high-sensitivity batches / generic Transformer-Jacobian-conditioning property, not a direct-EBM-parameterization-specific pathology). Secondary asymmetry (not primary evidence): cross-selection ratios weaker (direct on none's spikes=1.85, none on direct's spikes=1.22) -- grad_norm-based spike selection has a partial model-specific component even though own-selection magnitudes match. Layer localization mixed/inconsistent across blocks -- no clean 'which layer dominates' story. Table 1 validated the canonical residual identity to ~2e-7 relative error in both arms. CONCLUSION: residual-conditioned Jacobian amplification does NOT explain direct's growing-clip-rate instability at this tail depth (top-2.5%-of-960); deprioritize further tail-amplification probes, prioritize the causal single-lever tests (weight-decay 38070968, z-loss 38070989) and the FID-scale evaluation as deciding evidence. SUPERSEDED (2026-08-10, same session): external review caught that the primary interaction statistic compared each model on its OWN independently-selected batches (unmatched), not the source-matched contrast the design was built for. Back-of-envelope recompute on this run's own Table 3 numbers gives interaction ~0.45 log-units (~1.57x, OPPOSITE conclusion) using the correct pairing. Rerunning with the fixed statistic (commit b797524) plus early/mid/late checkpoint sweep -- do not cite this run's 'clean null' conclusion.
completed_runs.gate: does residual-conditioned Jacobian amplification A_backbone concentrate/spike specifically under direct on direct-selected spike batches (Hypothesis A), or is it shared across models (B), residual-driven (C), or a selection artifact (D)?

All 3 stages' CIs cross zero at n=24 spike/24 control -- underpowered, not a confirmed effect, but late-stage point estimate (0.456) closely reproduces the user's independent hand-derivation (0.452) from this run's own raw Table 3 numbers, a real consistency check. residual_ratio ~1.0 at every stage/model (0.986-1.045) -- grad_norm spike/control gap is carried by A (Jacobian amplification), not residual magnitude; |r|*A reconstructs the real grad_norm ratio to ~1-2%. Interaction I(t)=Delta_D-Delta_N (A-based): early +0.016 (CI [-0.101,0.315], null), mid -0.100 (CI [-0.223,0.050], null), late +0.321 (CI [0.008,0.654], EXCLUDES ZERO -- first significant single-checkpoint result in this investigation). I(late)-I(mid)=+0.421 (CI [0.069,0.769], excludes zero). G=I(late)-I(early)=+0.305 but CI [-0.066,0.688] still crosses zero (conservative independent-normal combination). grad-based late interaction +0.220 CI [-0.102,0.685] does NOT exclude zero -- A-based and grad-based metrics disagree on late-stage significance. residual_ratio~1.0 at every stage/model (0.994/1.016 at late) -- Hypothesis C (residual magnitude) again rejected, now at K=64. Table 7 tail quantiles: direct_own_spike tail_anisotropy_proxy(p99/p50)=7.73 vs direct_own_control=1.16, vs none_own_spike=2.34/none_own_control=1.15 -- direct's spike population has a much heavier RIGHT TAIL than none's, not just a higher median (median A_ratio ~2.5 similar between models). Phase 6/7 sigma_1/alignment (late stage, sv_k=8): on direct-selected batches, direct sigma_1_ratio(spike/control)=1.40 vs none=1.21 (both models' conditioning worsens somewhat, direct only modestly more); direct alignment_ratio=6.62 vs none=2.92 (more than 2x more direct-specific) -- the direct-specific excess is predominantly ALIGNMENT (residual/top-singular-vector alignment growing), not conditioning (sigma_1 growth is shared/modest in both arms). Points toward Mechanism 2 (worse alignment) as primary, Mechanism 1 (worse conditioning) secondary/shared. See documentation/longitudinal_jacobian_audit.md for checkpoint audit.

final_metric: Field-gain median vs k -- spike: k12=2.80 k24=1.56 k48=0.78 k96=0.69; control: k12=3.61 k24=2.19 k48=1.00 k96=0.70. k=12 medians reproduce Stage 2.5's 2.83/3.41 almost exactly, confirming k=12 truncation (not a bound violation) as the cause; gain collapses toward <=1 by k=96 on both. CAVEAT (unresolved): the tighter identity rho_m=-ell_m, exact to 1e-8 on the fp64 CPU synthetic test, does NOT hold tightly on the real fp32 GPU model -- identity_err stays 35-280 vs r_norm~500-600 (~20-45% relative) and GROWS with k rather than shrinking. Leading hypothesis (unverified): lambda_max here is huge (4-8e5, condition number 1e3-1e4), and single-reorthogonalization Lanczos in fp32 is known to lose orthogonality under this spectral spread at k~50-100, breaking the Q_m^T Q_m=I assumption the rho=-ell derivation needs -- without necessarily invalidating the independently-measured field-gain trend (read off a real re-application of A, not recurrence byproducts). Needs explicit ||Q^T Q - I|| reporting at large k to confirm before treating this as settled.

final_metric: DECISIVE: WFB's local quadratic model IS trustworthy at eta_alpha* -- rho stays near 1 across the {0.5,1,1.5}x bracket (spike medians 0.93/0.99/1.38; control 0.97/0.92/0.66), same-batch loss reliably decreases as predicted (median -1.0 to -1.4). HOWEVER: even WFB's well-linearized, locally-optimal step does NOT generalize -- probe_delta_L_median is POSITIVE at every bracket for BOTH alphas, frac_probe_improved=0.0 across all 12 (alpha x bracket x spike/control) cells. Single-batch Gauss-Newton-family steps appear to systematically overfit their own batch at this checkpoint (matches Stage 3 alpha=0 negative-control smoke's finding: probe loss also worsened despite 100% same-batch Armijo accept rate). Reading: WFB's GEOMETRY is locally sound (unlike FBGN's), but generalization requires the STOCHASTIC AVERAGING of many steps (standard SGD-family argument), not any single step -- informs Stage 3's 300-step run to judge on the PROBE-LOSS TRAJECTORY over many steps, not any individual step's sign.

Distinct from the earlier Lanczos-truncation pathology: this is a genuine finding about FBGN's Gauss-Newton direction applied via pure line search over many steps, not a numerical-methods bug. completed_runs.description: Stage 3A frozen-checkpoint mechanism discriminator: decides H1 (Gauss-Newton LOCAL-MODEL failure -> repair = LM damping) vs H2 (stochastic minibatch OVER-SOLVING -> repair = larger model batch / independent acceptance, damping cannot help) vs H3, for the certified CG-FBGN that reduced every one of its own minibatches while driving the deterministic probe 10.625 -> 14.881. No training/optimizer/parameter persistence: every candidate step is apply/evaluate/revert with BITWISE restoration asserted. Closes the two gaps the 300-step logs cannot: (1) eta-scan {1,1/2,1/4,1/8}xeta* at FIXED direction, separating step length from direction (the logged reduction ratio is confounded with step length); (2) the eta-INDEPENDENT infinitesimal transfer d_V = grad L_V . p on an independent 64-example trust bank -- d_V>=0 decides H2 outright since no step size or damping can rescue an ascent direction. Includes a norm-matched raw-direct control, true-residual CG certificates, and a folded-in lambda in {1,10,100}x sweep for H1. 3 checkpoints: start, FBGN step100, FBGN step300.
completed_runs.expected_runtime: ~2-3h (3 checkpoints x 8 model batches x 3 directions x 4 etas)
completed_runs.final_metric: start ckpt: FBGN C_V=0.00108 (vs raw-direct 0.0395), d_V descent 4/8, 8/8 trust batches worsen at eta*/8 (+0.063, ~4sigma); R_B -10.685 -> +0.910 and D_B 3.397 -> 0.459 as eta -> eta*/8; damping (10x/100x lam) drove C_V NEGATIVE. Verdict: H2 (stochastic over-solving) is causal; H1 is a trust-region artifact and its pre-registered repair FAILED its falsifier.
completed_runs.gate: H1/H2/H3 classification per the pre-registered rule in the discriminator docstring: H1 if median R_B<0.5 or median D_B>0.25 at eta* WHILE d_V<0; H2 if R_B~1 and D_B<<1 BUT d_V>=0 frequently or trust loss rises even at the smallest eta; H3 if both. Determines which (and only which) Stage 3B intervention is run.

completed_runs.description: Stage 3B batch-size discriminator for H2. 3 of the original 6 concurrent Stage2 jobs (structmask_seed0/34314943, gaussian_seed1/34315014, structmask_seed2/34315203) failed within a narrow ~14:00-14:04 EDT window -- structmask_seed0 and gaussian_seed1 both died mid-training (healthy loss trajectories right up to the failure, no traceback), structmask_seed2 died during dataset/VAE init. This correlated in time with this session's own SSH ControlMaster drop to the login node. Root-caused as NOT a code bug: gaussian_seed1 (plain, already-validated corruption mode) died the identical way as the structured_mask arm, and the other 3 concurrent jobs (gaussian_seed0, gm_seed0, structmask_seed1) ran through the same window unaffected -- consistent with a transient, node/session-specific network or auth blip, not a systemic or code-level issue. Separately, gm_seed2 (34315192, dependent via --dependency=afterany:34315014) failed instantly with Reason=Dependency once its dependency job failed -- this cluster's scheduler did not honor afterany's documented 'any terminal state' semantics for a FAILED dependency. And a first retry of gaussian_seed1 on gpu_test (34361882) was killed instantly (exit 0:53) by gpu_test's QOS MaxSubmitPU=2/MaxJobsPU=2 hard cap (confirmed via sacctmgr show qos) -- accepted by sbatch then killed by the scheduler rather than rejected at submission. All 4 affected arms retried on seas_gpu with no dependency clauses; all 4 retries pending cleanly. Process lesson: avoid --dependency=afterany chains on this cluster when the upstream job might fail, and avoid gpu_test for any 2nd+ concurrent submission given its MaxSubmitPU=2 cap (tighter than previously documented '~2 concurrent' -- confirmed exactly 2 via sacctmgr, submit-time not just run-time).

ROOT CAUSE of the mass Stage2 failure (6 jobs failed near-simultaneously ~14:49-15:20 EDT, including the long-running gaussian_seed0 control and its retries): train_stage2_structured_mask.sbatch shipped with --ckpt-every 5000 (copied verbatim from corruption_sanity.sbatch), saving a ~2GB step-checkpoint every 5000 steps IN ADDITION to the final epoch01.pt unconditional save -- Stage 2 only ever evaluates the single end-of-epoch checkpoint, so every intermediate save was pure waste. Across up to 8 concurrent/sequential 1-epoch arms this accumulated ~42GB of redundant checkpoints, filling home03's 95GB quota to exactly 100% (0 bytes free, confirmed via `quota -u mkrasnow /n/home03` and independently via a FASRC automated quota-warning email the user forwarded). This explains every observed symptom: the long-running gaussian_seed0 (34311555) stalled ~46min with no new log output once its next write hit the full disk, then died with exit code 1; freshly-submitted seas_gpu jobs died within ~10s (mkdir/log-file creation on a 100%-full NFS mount failing immediately); and the two jobs that survived the first wave (gm_seed0/34315003, structmask_seed1/34315015) died ~1h later via the identical stall-then-exit-1 pattern once THEY hit the full disk. This was NOT the SSH ControlMaster drop (that was coincidental/separate, and recovered independently each time) and NOT a code bug in structured_mask (the plain gaussian arm died identically). FIX: train_stage2_structured_mask.sbatch's --ckpt-every hardcoded to 5000 changed to ${CKPT_EVERY:-999999999} (disabled by default), matching train_stage1_longer.sbatch's own fix for the same root cause from Stage 1's incident #2. Cleaned up 20 stale step-checkpoints (~42GB) from home03, freeing it back to 33GB available. All 8 non-completed arms (only gaussian_seed2/34315134 fully completed) being retrained fresh with the fixed script. This is the 4th distinct home03/holylabs quota incident across Stage 1 and Stage 2 -- process lesson: any NEW sbatch script that trains for a fixed short duration and only needs the final checkpoint should default --ckpt-every to a very large number from the FIRST version, not retrofit it after an incident.

gates.cross_corruption_generalization: RESOLVED (2026-07-08) - built eval_generalization.py (new, per user request) testing whether gaussian+mask learns a genuinely general repair field vs memorizing its two exact training corruptions. All 6 checkpoints (gaussian, mask, 1:1, 1:2, 1:3, 1:4) evaluated on 9 unseen/composed corruptions (Bernoulli mask p=0.25/0.75/0.9 vs trained p=0.5, block mask, stroke mask, gaussian noise sigma=0.3/0.6/1.0, and noisy_masked -- a composition matching neither pure training distribution). KEY RESULT: on block_mask (recovery_mse), gaussian=0.768, mask-only=0.666, arm B(1:1)=0.649, 1:2=0.681, 1:3=0.668, 1:4=0.659. Only 1:1 and 1:4 beat BOTH pure arms simultaneously (genuine compositional generalization, not just interpolating between two memorized skills) -- 1:2 and 1:3 fall back above mask-only's floor despite having BETTER raw Pareto numbers (higher gap, lower FID) than 1:1. This is a real, non-monotonic tension: Pareto-optimality on trained corruptions and compositional generalization to novel corruptions are NOT the same axis and do not co-optimize cleanly across this ratio sweep. On noisy_masked, no mixture arm yet beats mask-only (0.160) -- gaussian=0.229, arm B=0.169, 1:2=0.163, 1:3=0.171, 1:4=0.166, all mixtures beat gaussian but not mask-only. Field-ordering (ordering_holds) is best for arm B AND 1:4 (both 8/9, fail only mask_p0.9), better than gaussian (4/9), mask-only (5/9), and 1:2/1:3 (7/9 each, fail mask_p0.9 and gaussian_sigma1.0). Corrected 2026-07-08: an earlier draft of this entry miscounted arm B as 6/9 and 1:4 as a 'perfect 9/9' -- both wrong, verified by direct recount from raw JSON; both are actually tied at 8/9. Smoke-sample-probe not separately re-run for this eval (reuses the same GD sampler/checkpoints already validated by generation_quality_fid).
gates.energy_ordering: RESOLVED (2026-07-07) - field-norm proxy (||f(x)||, since ebm=none has no scalar energy head) on gaussian/mask/arm-B checkpoints, n=256, mask_prob=0.5. Checks E(clean) < E(corrupt) < E(noise) per CLAUDE.md diagnostic 3. clean < corrupt holds for all three arms (all recognize near-manifold states as low-field). But corrupt vs noise ordering ONLY holds for arm B (gaussian+mask): gaussian floor has corrupt=304.2 > noise=250.1 (FAILS, never trained on masked states -- off-distribution), mask-only has corrupt=202.6 > noise=182.3 (FAILS, never trained on pure noise -- off-distribution), arm B has corrupt=199.9 < noise=248.4 (HOLDS). This is a SECOND, mechanistically independent line of evidence for the same generalization argument as generation_quality_fid: training on both corruption types produces a model whose field response is well-calibrated across the whole state space, not just one whose FID happens to be preserved. Single-arm checkpoints each show a specific off-distribution failure mode matching exactly what they were never trained on.

gates.step3_fourier_sanity: RESOLVED, NEGATIVE (2026-07-06) - isolated fourier-corruption training (fourier-cutoff=0.25), same eval protocol as step2. mean_masked_mse=0.40612, WORSE than gaussian floor (0.24237). normalized_gap=-0.720 (negative -- fourier-trained model is worse at masked-recovery than a model that never saw structured corruption at all). Mechanism read: fourier low-pass corruption teaches recovery of missing HIGH-FREQUENCY detail from coarse structure, not recovery of a spatially-masked region from surrounding visible pixels -- these are different tasks, and training on one does not transfer to (and may actively hurt, via distribution mismatch) the other. USER DECISION 2026-07-07: fourier dropped from build path entirely (option a of pi-updates.md ask).
gates.step4_mixture_arm_B: RESOLVED (2026-07-06) - 2-way gaussian+mask mixture (weights 1.0/1.0/0.0), same eval protocol. mean_masked_mse=0.13692, normalized_gap=0.464. Falls between isolated mask (0.568) and 3-arm mixture (0.449) as expected, but notably closer to the 3-arm mixture than to isolated mask -- confirms the 3-arm mixture's underperformance vs isolated mask is NOT primarily fourier-specific drag (arm B still loses ~0.10 gap vs pure mask despite excluding fourier entirely). Read together with step3's negative fourier result: the gap-closing recipe (gaussian:mask:fourier 1:1:1 vs 1:1:0 vs mask-only) suggests BOTH effects are real -- gradient-budget dilution (any mixing with gaussian reduces the pure-mask signal) AND fourier's own negative contribution. Fourier's negative pull is smaller in magnitude here (only 1/3 weight) than shown by its isolated -0.720 result, consistent with a real but diluted drag.
